acceptance_requirements: candidate identifier reconstructs from source, dimension, target and rule
source work exists exactly once in the canonical input
registered inclusion pattern matches each governed title or substantive notes evidence value independently
registered exclusion pattern does not match within the same declared evidence field
a jurisdiction-qualified organisation literal resolves only to its separately registered jurisdiction-specific rule and official identity target
a retired generic entity rule remains absent where its literal spans public systems in multiple jurisdictions but its former target represented only one
a prefix- or suffix-qualified name for a distinct bank, agency, commission or tribunal cannot support the shorter entity rule
the Montserrat constitutional context abstains without suppressing the separately calibrated UK Electoral Commission founding context
every evidence row preserves its exact source field, raw source value, canonical-JSON value hash, matched literal and governed field provenance
evidence value is an exact case-insensitive substring of the normalized declared source field
one candidate deduplicates stable title and notes support for the same source, dimension, target and rule
category, document_type, publisher_title and tags are inspected but cannot support a subject or entity candidate under the governed snapshot profile
topic candidates are not already source-declared and are not in the fail-closed v1 suppression set
concept and entity targets are registered in the controlled vocabulary
authority is model-assisted derived discovery metadata
rights and freshness metadata are present
candidate does not claim official legal classification or legal advice
terminal_outcome_requirements: exactly one terminal outcome exists for every canonical work
topic, concept and entity-link attempt outcomes are explicit
title, notes, category, document_type, publisher_title and tags each record considered status, exact value hash, governed dimensions, evaluation outcome and supporting candidate identifiers
candidate identifiers referenced by an outcome join exactly
abstention is used where no literal supported candidate exists
metadata-only candidate count is exactly zero
CLML remains an explicit abstention while no frozen body is bound
limitations: Policy review and deterministic reconstruction are not qualified legal-practitioner assurance.
A literal-rule match is discovery metadata, not an official legal classification.
An abstention is not evidence that a work lacks a topic, concept or entity.
The Codex task surface does not expose exact deployment identity, sampling parameters, subscription token usage, weekly allowance usage or attributable subscription cost.
